b3_framing_correction.right: C1 and C2 did their retrieval job -- candidate CES rose at every scale and the availability targets were met. What failed is the COMPOSITION: large candidate pool + current S2. That distinction determines what gets built next, which is why it is recorded explicitly.
b3_framing_correction.wrong: C1 and C2 are failed retrieval policies.

decision_rule.P2_far_below_P3_ceiling: a runtime-safe compressor cannot approach what an oracle compressor achieves -> go to the runtime graph rather than piling heuristics into the prefilter
decision_rule.P2_holds_availability_but_efficiency_sta: pressure is not the whole story; S2's discrimination is inadequate independent of set size -> selector-capacity work, not more compression
decision_rule.P2_restores_efficiency_and_holds_availab: selector pressure WAS the mechanism -> freeze prefilter + C2, then run HRM
decision_rule.P2_restores_efficiency_only_by_discardin: the prefilter is solving the wrong problem -> reject it

if_b4_fails: Move directly to runtime-graph expansion rather than adding further heuristics to S2. The graph is then judged against the prefilter on: initial retrieval size, candidates reaching S2, bridge availability, plausible bridge count, selected CES, and cost.

P1.role: the known overload control; reproduces the B3 failure

P3.pipeline: C2 expanded retrieval -> ORACLE prefilter to M -> S2
P3.role: PREFILTER CEILING: bounds what any compressor could achieve

new_metrics_frozen.why_frozen_now: B3 gives direct evidence that selector performance deteriorates as structural competition explodes, so the ratio becomes a first-class metric rather than a post-hoc explanation.

only_new_mechanism: the prefilter in P2. S2 is unchanged, retrieval is C2 as already measured, packet stays 6.

packet_budget.why: Raising it might improve Q while erasing the scientific question -- one could no longer tell whether the fix was better selection or simply more working context.

prefilter_runtime_safety.enforcement: same discipline as selector_v2: a test strips docstrings and comments and asserts no executable statement references a forbidden field.

primary_criteria.bridge_conditional_retention: P2 delta vs P0 >= -0.05 at EVERY scale, the same bound and the same per-scale requirement that exposed the B3 floor effect
primary_criteria.competition: structural and bridge competition ratios must fall materially versus P1
primary_criteria.role_availability_after_prefilter: bridge and terminal availability must not fall more than 0.05 below the pre-prefilter (C2) level -- compression must not undo the availability B3 bought
primary_criteria.selected_ces_given_available: P2 must materially exceed P1 and approach P0's efficiency (P0 sits at 0.82-0.97; P1 collapses to 0.17-0.25)

question: Can we preserve the evidence availability gained by expanded retrieval while reducing the structurally plausible candidate set enough that UNCHANGED S2 regains its development-level discrimination?

METRIC_TRAP_FOUND_AND_CORRECTED.correction: The honest end-to-end figure is prefilter_ces x selected_ces_given_working. Reported below as the primary comparison.
METRIC_TRAP_FOUND_AND_CORRECTED.trap: selected_ces_given_working is CONDITIONED on the prefilter's own coverage, so it RISES as the prefilter discards evidence. P2 at M=25 posts 0.785 on that metric at cal_3000 -- the best number in the whole table -- while having thrown away half the required evidence before S2 ever saw it.
METRIC_TRAP_FOUND_AND_CORRECTED.why_it_matters: Reading the conditional metric alone would have declared P2@M25 a triumph and promoted a compressor that merely matches the old k=50 baseline.

result_2026_08_09.M_trend_is_informative: Smaller M is BETTER for P2 end-to-end (M25 > M50 > M75) purely because a smaller working set concentrates S2, while larger M readmits the competition. But P3 shows the same ordering, so the gain is about pressure, not about my filter improving with size. Both suggest the working set wants to be small AND well chosen -- P2 achieves only the first.

P2_RESULT_my_compressor_is_inadequate.but_coverage_collapsed: prefilter CES falls from 0.833-0.860 (P1) to 0.433-0.540 at M=25 -- roughly half the availability B3 bought is destroyed in compression. Bridge availability after prefilter falls to 0.385-0.821 versus P3's 0.873-0.931 at the same M.
P2_RESULT_my_compressor_is_inadequate.net_effect: end-to-end selected CES at M=25 merely MATCHES P0 (0.340 vs 0.340 at cal_3000, 0.380 vs 0.387 at cal_1500). The expanded retrieval plus my compressor buys nothing over plain k=50.
P2_RESULT_my_compressor_is_inadequate.pressure_reduction_worked: structural competition ratio falls from 8.8 to 1.5 at cal_1500 and 17.3 to 1.5 at cal_3000; bridge competition 3.9 -> 1.1. Near-duplicate suppression collapses 20.7-26.8 records per task. So the mechanism DOES relieve the diagnosed pressure.
P2_RESULT_my_compressor_is_inadequate.verdict: FAIL. It reduces pressure successfully but pays for it by discarding required evidence.

result_2026_08_09.P3_RESULT_compression_is_viable: The oracle compressor recovers strongly: end-to-end selected CES 0.620/0.540/0.507/0.513/0.473 at M=25, versus P1's 0.353/0.287/0.153/0.160/0.120 and P0's 0.493/0.393/0.387/0.320/0.340. So a perfect compressor lets UNCHANGED S2 both keep the availability B3 bought AND select from it -- roughly 1.4x the k=50 baseline at every scale, and 3-4x P1 at the large scales. Compression is the right shape of intervention, and S2 is not irreparably broken.
result_2026_08_09.diagnosis: The two-opposing-quantities scoring did its job: it separated 'reduced pressure' from 'kept the evidence' and showed my compressor achieves the first by sacrificing the second. Structure-as-admissibility was too coarse a filter -- 'mentions the subject OR the relation OR a one-hop entity OR looks like an identity record' admits far more than M records at these pool sizes, so the retrieval-score ranking inside the admitted set decides what survives, and retrieval score is precisely the signal that already failed to rank the bridge highly. The compressor inherits the retriever's blind spot rather than correcting it.
result_2026_08_09.next: Either a better runtime-safe discriminator (relation-typed matching, subject-anchored path scoring, role-aware reservation) or the runtime graph. P3 gives the ceiling to beat and P2 gives the floor a new mechanism must clear.
result_2026_08_09.per_frozen_decision_rule: 'P3 succeeds but P2 fails -> compression is viable; the runtime-safe compressor needs better discrimination.' Recorded as exactly that. Not a licence to widen M, weaken the bound, or raise the packet.
result_2026_08_09.status: P3 SUCCEEDS, P2 FAILS. Per the frozen decision rule: compression is VIABLE, but the runtime-safe compressor needs better discrimination. No arm promoted, no HRM run.
result_2026_08_09.what_this_says_about_the_graph: P3 proves a compressor that KNOWS which records matter unlocks S2. The runtime cannot know that from retrieval score plus coarse structural admissibility. A runtime graph is precisely a mechanism for identifying which records matter STRUCTURALLY rather than by score -- reaching the bridge by relation-aware traversal instead of hoping it ranks well. The P3-minus-P2 gap (0.473 vs 0.340 at cal_3000) is now a measured budget for what better discrimination is worth.

scored_on_two_opposing_quantities.pressure_reduction: the structurally plausible competition must actually fall
scored_on_two_opposing_quantities.recall_into_prefiltered_set: required evidence, and each ROLE, must survive compression -- a prefilter that discards the bridge has solved nothing
scored_on_two_opposing_quantities.the_target_shape: expanded pool 300 candidates / ~24 plausible bridges -> prefiltered 50 candidates / ~5 plausible bridges -> S2 selects 6. High role availability retained WHILE competition collapses is the missing middle layer.

why_this_and_not_graph_retrieval_yet: The graph direction is now empirically motivated, not speculative -- but a prefilter is the SMALLEST causal intervention that isolates the diagnosed cause. It answers 'is S2 failing merely because it is handed too many plausible records at once?' WITHOUT simultaneously changing the retrieval architecture. Changing both would leave the attribution ambiguous in exactly the way B3's 2x2 was built to avoid.

working_set_size_M.rationale: A small prospective set is enough to tell whether selector PRESSURE is the mechanism. A broad grid would convert a mechanism test into hyperparameter search.
